title: The dispatcher swap retires a Uniboost still holding retained prime and never sweeps it — 20.03 USDC locally, a quarter of it created by the fix itself — and the mainnet twin `_swapUniboost` has the same no-sweep shape on live positions
fingerprintNote: Accepted VERBATIM as supplied by dedup. NOT recomputed by finding-manager. The fingerprint is the only collision-proof key for this record; the label L-xx/Q-xx is run-scoped and collides with run-21 and run-26 labels on this same entry point.
description: `Uniboost._dispatch` streams `donationSplit%` of the dispatched prime to the recipient and RETAINS the remainder for a later `pool()` (Uniboost.sol:222-238; split is 50). `_accrueIndex1MintDebt` now deterministically drives one extra index-1 mint on every local run, adding to that retained balance, and Phase 7.6 retires the holder moments later with no sweep and no assertion about its balance. Measured on chain after a clean run: the retired incumbent 0xdbC43Ba45381e02825b14322cDdd15eC4B3164E6 holds 20030020 (20.030020 USDC) — exactly 50% of four index-1 mints at prices 10000000 + 10010000 + 10020010 + 10030030 — of which 5015015 (25%) was created by story-079's own accrual mint; the remaining 15015015 pre-existed the fix. So the change did not invent the residue, it converted a live retained balance on the LIVE dispatcher into a residue on an OFF-INDEX one. The replacement starts at zero retained prime (verified: USDC.balanceOf(new) == 0 immediately post-swap). Recoverability was probed rather than assumed: `Uniboost.rescueERC20(USDC, deployer, 20030020)` against the retired contract returned status 0x1 and left balance 0, and `pool()` remains callable there (poolerAuthVersion(MultiPooler) == authVersion == 1, owner still the deployer). The value is PARKED, not lost. The cross-artifact half is the reason this is worth recording: mainnet `_swapUniboost` (DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol:1443-1538) has no sweep either, and its indices 1/2/3 incumbents are live dispatchers that have been accumulating real retained USDC from real user mints. That magnitude is NOT measured here — `dev` targets a fresh anvil and no mainnet fork was in scope for this entry point — so the mainnet leg of this finding is tagged unverified.
impact: Local: cosmetic, a small residue on a disposable chain. Mainnet (unverified magnitude): after the cutover the retained-prime pot silently splits across two addresses; any pooling automation bound to the address-book dispatcher calls `pool()` on a contract whose retained balance is zero and reverts `"Uniboost: nothing to pool"` until fresh mints accrue, while the real balance sits on a retired contract nothing points at. Recoverable in one owner transaction once noticed.
attackPath: 1. Not an attack path — an operational-hazard path. No adversary is required or asserted.
2. `_rehearseDispatcherSwap` retires the incumbent Uniboost with a non-zero retained prime balance and no sweep or assertion.
3. The address book and every consumer repoint to the replacement, whose retained balance is zero.
4. Pooling automation targeting the address-book dispatcher reverts `Uniboost: nothing to pool`; the operator looks for the pot at the address the address book names and does not find it there.
5. Recovery: one owner `rescueERC20` on the retired contract — proved to work locally.
recommendation: In DeployMocks Phase 7.6, snapshot `IERC20(rewardToken).balanceOf(oldUb)` before the swap and, after `replaceDispatcher`, either sweep it to the replacement (`oldUb.rescueERC20(rewardToken, address(newUb), residue)`) or assert it is zero — so the local rehearsal actually exercises the decision instead of leaving it implicit. More importantly, carry the question to the promotion-ready entry point: before the mainnet cutover, read each incumbent Uniboost's prime balance and decide explicitly whether to sweep it to the replacement or leave it for a later `rescueERC20`; whichever is chosen, assert the end state so the pot's location is recorded rather than discovered. Recommend a fork-based measurement of the mainnet incumbents' balances as part of that entry point's audit.
severityRationale: Not High: nothing is stolen, lost or compromised — recoverability was demonstrated, not assumed, so this is not asset loss under any reading. Not Medium: no protocol function or availability is impacted on the artifact actually audited (chain 31337, mock token), and this is expressly NOT a value leak — parked value under a proven one-transaction owner recovery is misplacement, not leakage. Not suppressed to QA either, and the reason is Law 3: the consequence is NON-OBVIOUS. A competent, non-malicious operator would reasonably assume the dispatcher the address book names is the dispatcher holding the retained pot, and would be surprised to learn the pot stayed behind on a retired contract. Surprise implies footgun, and footguns are in scope at honest severity — which here is Low, because the surprise costs a lookup and one transaction, not an asset.
severityRationaleAsProposed: Proposed Low. Explicitly NOT a value leak: recoverability was proved empirically (rescueERC20 returned the full balance), the owner is trusted per Law 3, and on chain 31337 the token is a mock. It stays a reportable Low rather than being suppressed because the consequence is non-obvious — a competent operator would reasonably assume the address-book dispatcher carries the pot — which is the footgun test under Law 3.

classification.assetImpact: Local: none — 20.030020 of a MOCK USDC on chain 31337, and recoverability was PROVED rather than assumed (`Uniboost.rescueERC20(USDC, deployer, 20030020)` returned status 0x1 and left the balance at 0; `pool()` remains callable there, poolerAuthVersion(MultiPooler) == authVersion == 1, owner still the deployer). The value is PARKED, not lost. Explicitly NOT filed as a value leak.
classification.whatActuallyBreaks: The rehearsal retires a value-holding contract without ever deciding, in code, what happens to the value it holds — no sweep, no assertion, not even a balance read. `Uniboost._dispatch` retains `100 - donationSplit`% of every dispatched prime for a later `pool()` (Uniboost.sol:222-238, split 50), and `_accrueIndex1MintDebt` now deterministically adds one more index-1 mint to that balance on every local run. Measured post-run: the retired incumbent 0xdbC43Ba45381e02825b14322cDdd15eC4B3164E6 holds 20030020 — exactly 50% of four index-1 mints at prices 10000000 + 10010000 + 10020010 + 10030030 — of which 5015015 (25%) was created by story-079's own accrual mint and 15015015 pre-existed. The change did not invent the residue; it converted a live retained balance on the LIVE dispatcher into a residue on an OFF-INDEX one. The replacement starts at zero retained prime (verified).
classification.whatAnOperatorGainsOrLoses: Nothing is gained by anyone. What an operator loses is knowledge of where the pot is: after the cutover the retained-prime pot silently splits across two addresses, and any pooling automation bound to the address-book dispatcher calls `pool()` on a contract whose retained balance is zero and reverts `Uniboost: nothing to pool` until fresh mints accrue, while the real balance sits on a retired contract nothing points at. Recoverable in one owner transaction once noticed.
attackPath: 1. Not an attack path — an operational-hazard path. No adversary is required or asserted.
2. `_rehearseDispatcherSwap` retires the incumbent Uniboost with a non-zero retained prime balance and no sweep or assertion.
3. The address book and every consumer repoint to the replacement, whose retained balance is zero.
4. Pooling automation targeting the address-book dispatcher reverts `Uniboost: nothing to pool`; the operator looks for the pot at the address the address book names and does not find it there.
5. Recovery: one owner `rescueERC20` on the retired contract — proved to work locally.
classification.likelihood: Certain on the local chain (measured). On mainnet the SHAPE is confirmed present — `_swapUniboost` (DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol:1443-1538) has no sweep either, and its indices 1/2/3 incumbents are live dispatchers accumulating real retained USDC from real user mints — but the MAGNITUDE is unmeasured and out of scope for this entry point.
classification.assumptions: That the retained-prime accounting behaves on mainnet as it does locally, and that the owner retains the `rescueERC20` capability and Uniboost ownership at cutover time.
classification.externalRequirements: For any mainnet consequence: a mainnet cutover must actually execute, and the incumbent must hold a non-trivial retained balance at that moment. Neither is established by this entry point.

escalationTrigger: Raise to MEDIUM if a fork measurement at the promotion-ready entry point shows a mainnet incumbent holding a materially non-trivial retained prime balance AND ANY of: recovery is not a single owner transaction (rescueERC20 unavailable, ownership transferred or renounced, or a poolerAuthVersion / authVersion mismatch making `pool()` unreachable on the retired contract); or the pooling automation's revert is persistent enough to halt a distribution the protocol depends on (availability impact rather than an inconvenience). Raise to HIGH only if the retained balance is shown to be genuinely unrecoverable — at that point it is asset loss, not misplacement.
law3: ASSESSED AND RETAINED as a reportable non-obvious operational hazard, not suppressed as owner trust and not framed as owner malice. No malicious-owner vector is asserted anywhere in this finding. The footgun test is met: the operator is surprised by where the value ends up. Safe-config guidance is carried in `recommendation` (snapshot the balance before the swap and either sweep it to the replacement or assert it is zero, so the pot's location is recorded rather than discovered).

poc.reason: C4 requires a coded PoC for High/Medium only. Severity here is low.
